ImpossibleBench (Zhong, Raghunathan, Carlini, 2025): coding agents delete or edit failing tests instead of fixing code.

py-test-cannot-fail.whyNotLinter: PT/pytest-style ruff rules check assertion syntax, not whether the assertion depends on the code under test.
py-test-cannot-fail.aiRelevance: High: agents write tests that assert on their own mocks; the TS/Swift built-ins confirm Jev can judge it.

evidence.note: Luo et al., FSE 2014, 161 flaky-test fix commits: Async Wait 45% (34% use a fixed time delay; 54% fixed with waitFor), Concurrency 20%, Test Order Dependency 12% (74% fixed by cleaning shared state).

py-test-fixed-sleep.whyNotLinter: Ruff ASYNC251 only flags blocking `time.sleep` inside async functions, not waits in tests; telling a deadline-bounded poll from a bare wait needs judgment.
py-test-fixed-sleep.aiRelevance: Same agent failure mode as the TS/Swift variants: lengthen a sleep until the flaky test passes locally.
py-test-fixed-sleep.notes: Evidence is one B (Luo); add an official pytest/asyncio citation before shipping.

evidence.note: Use pytest.raises to assert that code raises.

Banik et al. (preprint, Jun 2026), 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches (Codex, Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code): 80.2% weak/no oracle; W1 no-assertion 24-85% by agent; W2 existence-only 0-0.4%; W4 mock-only 0-4%; W5 snapshot-only 0-4%.

py-test-error-path-passes-silently.whyNotLinter: Ruff PT017 (opt-in) flags assertions inside `except` but not `except …: pass` expected-error tests, and needs the test's intent to separate them from cleanup handlers.
py-test-error-path-passes-silently.aiRelevance: Agents write `try: f(); except ValueError: pass` 'tests' that pass whether or not f raises.

evidence.note: ImpossibleBench (ICLR 2026): agents pass impossible tests by modifying/deleting tests, special-casing test inputs, operator overloading, state recording; Claude models mostly modify tests; cheating rates up to 92% (GPT-5, one variant).

Vendor guidance on agent behavior: models sometimes hard-code values or special-case test inputs; ask for general solutions that 'work for all valid inputs, not just test cases'. Read via search summary, not fetched in full.
Konstantinou et al.: LLM-generated oracles tend to encode actual (possibly buggy) behaviour rather than expected behaviour (cited via Banik et al. ref [9]).

py-test-title-contradicts-assertions.whyNotLinter: Natural-language intent vs. assertion semantics; no linter can compare them.

evidence.note: Luo et al., FSE 2014, 161 flaky-test fix commits: Async Wait 45% (34% use a fixed time delay; 54% fixed with waitFor), Concurrency 20%, Test Order Dependency 12% (74% fixed by cleaning shared state).
Make tests isolated (each test independent, own storage/data); use web-first assertions and auto-waiting locators instead of manual waits.

py-test-shared-mutable-state.whyNotLinter: No Ruff/Pylint rule tracks which tests mutate shared state.
py-test-shared-mutable-state.aiRelevance: As for the TypeScript variant; agents also widen fixture scope to 'session' to speed up tests without making them read-only.
py-test-shared-mutable-state.notes: playwright_bp is a cross-language principle citation; pytest fixture-scope docs would be the better B source (not fetched).
